confirmed.title: Middle-initial and name-form variants split 456 author IDs into 225 duplicate identities
confirmed.claim: Exact name_key matching splits the same person across multiple author_ids whenever the byline adds/drops a middle initial, reorders a surname particle, or uses a leading initial. 456 of 6,140 article authors (7.4%) are duplicate IDs of 225 real people, affecting 1,040/10,858 article slots (9.6%) and 1,405/8,331 unique coauthor edges (16.9%).
confirmed.evidence: Union-find over authors joined to article non-duplicate authorships (SELECT author_id, given_name, family_name FROM authors; COUNT(*) FROM authorships a JOIN papers p USING(paper_id) WHERE p.content_type='article' AND p.is_duplicate=0). Final counts after adding leading-initial compatibility: 225 clusters touching articles, 456 article author IDs, 231 excess ghost identities, corrected 5,909 article authors (3.76% overcount), 1,040 article slots (9.58%), 1,405/8,331 unique coauthor edges (16.86%); per-paper pair occurrences 1,637/9,393 (17.43%). No paper has two IDs from the same cluster (0 same-person pairs). Examples by slots: Parag A Pathak #1025 (16) / Parag Pathak #3012 (2); James A Robinson #1080 (16) / James Robinson #959 (1); Michael Kremer #332 (15) / Michael R Kremer #1252 (1); John J Siegfried #170 (9) / John Siegfried #173 (6); David H Autor #790 (7) / David Autor #2001 (7); Abhijit V Banerjee #422/#764/#5171; Steven D Levitt #241/#286/#807. Ten surname-particle groups: John Van Reenen #1413/#3089, Till von Wachter #1385/#1926, Pedro Dal Bo #1154/#2788, Jan De Loecker #3329/#3905, Gopi Shah Goda #2903/#3002, Eric van Wincoop #362/#2932, Eric Van den Steen #878/#3979, Eliana La Ferrara #639/#1627, Bram De Rock #3368/#3899, Arthur van Soest #1439/#2813. Three leading-initial pairs: Vernon Henderson #2831 / J. Vernon Henderson #3110; H. Peyton Young #2112 / Peyton Young #5930; W. Reed Walker #2847 / Reed Walker #3928. Manual review of about 30 pairs found one genuine distinct-namesake pair: Robert L Clark #735 (NC State) vs Robert Clark #3875 (HEC Montreal/Queen's), so merge precision is about 95%, not 100%.

confirmed.title: published_month is one month earlier than the AEA issue cover month for 1,495 records (2002-2009)
confirmed.claim: 1,495 of 5,498 records (27.2%) have published_month exactly one month earlier than the AEA issue cover month. Every mismatch falls in 2002-2009, where 73.8%-96.7% of records per year are affected, while 2000-2001 and 2010-2026 have zero mismatches. The publication year is unaffected.
confirmed.evidence: Joined every DB paper on (volume, issue) to the AEA issues index at https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/issues (234 issues, volumes 89-116): 4,003 exact month matches and 1,495 mismatches, every mismatch DB = AEA minus one month. Examples: 10.1257/000282803321455133 (Lucas, 'Macroeconomic Priorities') DB 2003-02 vs AEA Vol. 93 No. 1 March 2003; 10.1257/000282806776157759 (Diamond-Rajan, 'Money in a Theory of Banking') DB 2006-02 vs AEA Vol. 96 No. 1 March 2006. docs/data-sources.md line 57 warns only that issue-level analysis is less safe than year-level; it does not disclose this offset.

confirmed.likely_cause: Crossref issued/published date appears to record the online/deposit month while AEA issue metadata records the cover month; AEA deposit practice seems to change after 2001 and again after 2009.
confirmed.recommended_fix: Decide the semantics of published_month: align it to the AEA cover month for 2002-2009, or add a separate issue_cover_month/online_month column and document which date M2 career timing uses. Do not use the current field for issue-level joins until reconciled.

confirmed.likely_cause: The M1 content-type classifier is title-exact and year-inconsistent; it recognizes some administrative titles in some years but not others, and has no rule for the 'Report of the Editor' family or for records with roman-numeral pages.
confirmed.recommended_fix: Extend the classifier with a curated administrative-title list and a roman-numeral/issue-back-matter rule; retype these 51 records (mostly to association_report or front_matter), recompute is_pp and all downstream counts, and make the rule year-independent. Re-run the quality report, which currently publishes the inflated 4,844/1,847/10,858.

confirmed.evidence: Raw-page scan found 45 suffix records across 45 distinct DOIs, representing 29 distinct given+family+suffix names. Examples: 10.1257/000282803321455133 (AEA 'Lucas Jr., Robert E.', DB 'Robert E Lucas'); 10.1257/0002828041302091 (John J Donohue III); 10.1257/aer.96.3.499 (Wilbur John Coleman II). Three names appear both with and without a suffix (roland g fryer, james peoples, joseph e harrington). 43 of the 45 suffix records are on content_type='article' papers (some of them the misclassified front matter in F6).
confirmed.likely_cause: The authorship schema omits a suffix column and the name-key normalizer discards Crossref suffix values.
confirmed.recommended_fix: Add suffix to authorships/authors, backfill from the cached raw Crossref pages, include it in canonical_name/display and optionally in the name key; keep suffix out of the primary name key where it would split one person.

confirmed.title: 41 non-research records are classified as content_type='article'
confirmed.claim: 41 article-classified records are not research articles: 17 'Foreword', 17 Editors'/Editor's Introduction, 4 American Economic Journal announcements, 1 'Journal of Economic Literature', 1 'Editor, Journal of Economic Literature' and 1 'REPORT OF INDEPENDENT AUDITOR'. They carry 57 author slots and 27 distinct authors, inflating the reported research-article count (4,844) by 0.85% and creating phantom publications and coauthorship for M2.
confirmed.evidence: Title-pattern scan over all content_type='article' rows returned exactly 41 hits. Examples: 10.1257/aer.99.2.671 ('Journal of Economic Literature'), 10.1257/aer.99.2.676 ('American Economic Journal: Applied Economics'), 10.1257/aer.106.5.xi ('Foreword'), 10.1257/aer.112.6.2083 ('REPORT OF INDEPENDENT AUDITOR'). Many use roman-numeral page DOIs (.vii/.viii/.ix/.x/.xi).
confirmed.likely_cause: The content-type classifier relies on Crossref type/title heuristics and does not catch AEA front-matter items deposited as journal-article with roman-numeral page DOIs.
confirmed.recommended_fix: Extend the classifier with these title/page patterns and reclassify as front_matter or association_report; recompute article counts, author cohorts and network statistics.

(1) 10 of the 41 are hidden duplicate deposits of 10 of the others: for each of 2002-2006 both the Foreword and the Editors'/Editor's Introduction exist twice in the same volume/issue - a legacy 10.1257/000282... record with numeric pages 7/8/9 and a modern 10.1257/aer.VV.I.vii/viii/ix record with roman pages (pairs 25/5028, 247/5030, 448/5056, 690/5034, 839/5036, 1/5027, 246/5029, 513/5055, 729/5033, 845/5035). detect_duplicates missed them because apostrophes/title and page representations differ; all 10 remain in content_type='article' and in the 4,844. The finding's row-level count and its 41/4,844=0.85% statement are nonetheless exactly right; the duplicate-pair issue is an additional defect, not a refutation. (2) The count is a lower bound: at least 10 more obvious non-research records are content_type='article' outside the six patterns - 10.1257/aer.99.2.674 (Journal of Economic Perspectives announcement), 10.1257/000282806777211784 (Editor, Journal of Economic Perspectives), 10.1257/0002828041302271 (John Bates Clark Award), 10.1257/aer.98.2.559 (John Bates Clark Medalist), 10.1257/aer.99.2.646 / 10.1257/aer.101.3.668 / 10.1257/aer.102.3.635 (List of Online Reports), and 10.1257/aer.99.2.712 / 10.1257/aer.100.2.719 / 10.1257/aer.101.3.747 (General Information on the Association), so the full defect class is at least 51 rows (1.05% of 4,844) and the recommended fix scoped to the six patterns would leave >=10 misclassified rows. (4) Relative impact on the reported P&P article count is larger than on the overall article count: 40/1,847 = 2.17%. confirmed.title: Duplicate detection misses 16 of 67 duplicate pairs (recall 76.1%)
confirmed.claim: The dedup pass marks 51 pairs (all in 96(4)/97(1) legacy-vs-modern), but 16 pairs of records with the same work remain both non-duplicate. 10 are P&P front-matter pairs, 3 are other front-matter pairs, 2 are research articles, and 1 is an erratum pair. Because both records stay canonical, downstream counts double-count these works and author identities.
confirmed.evidence: Read-only SQL audit. detect_duplicates scans only content_type='article' and requires exact equality on LOWER(TRIM(title)), published_year, volume, issue, page_first, page_last (src/econpub/classify.py). Marked pairs: 51 (24 in 96(4), 27 in 97(1)). Normalized-title+page+author inventory found 67 duplicate pairs (51 marked, 16 unmarked = 32 records): 10 P&P front-matter pairs (1/5027, 25/5028, 246/5029, 247/5030, 513/5055, 448/5056, 729/5033, 690/5034, 839/5035, 845/5036), 3 front-matter pairs (3486/3499, 3657/3664, 4040/4047), 2 research pairs (1050/4062, 1064/4063), 1 erratum pair (1005/4092). 96(4) legacy: 26 records, 24 marked; unmatched 4087 'Abstracts' (no modern counterpart) and 4092 (duplicates 1005). 97(1) legacy: 30 records, 27 marked; unmatched 4062, 4063, 4077 'Abstracts' (no modern counterpart). Recall 51/67 = 76.1%.

4040 10.1257/aer.107.3.i (i-vi) vs 4047 '10.1257/aer.107.3.i;' (1-6); raw DOI ends with a semicolon and URL is https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.107.3.i;.

confirmed.title: AEA institution metadata is empty for 2002-2007; Crossref affiliations are the only usable M2 source
confirmed.claim: On sampled AEA pages, citation_author_institution is essentially absent for 2002-2007 (2/31 author slots) while Crossref has 30/31; over the full sample AEA supplies 105/134 slots vs Crossref 134/134. Outside 2002-2007 AEA provides mostly abbreviated institution names. M2 should build career-stage features from Crossref publish-time affiliation strings, not AEA institution scraping.
confirmed.evidence: Pooled 2002-2007 AEA vs Crossref slot comparison 2/31 vs 30/31; full sample 105/134 vs 134/134. Crossref research-article affiliation coverage is 10,773/10,858 = 99.2% corpus-wide and 97.6%-98.7% in each year 2002-2007.
examples: 2002-2007 pooled: AEA 2/31 vs Crossref 30/31 affiliation slots
Full sample: AEA 105/134 vs Crossref 134/134
2000-2001 and 2008+ AEA institutions are abbreviated names only
confirmed.likely_cause: AEA HTML templates for 2002-2007 do not emit citation_author_institution; later templates emit abbreviated names.
confirmed.recommended_fix: Use Crossref affiliation strings for M2 rank/career extraction; use AEA institutions only as a 2008+ cross-check and record affiliation_source. Do not plan an AEA-only affiliation backfill for 2002-2007.

votes.evidence:
Reproduced exactly. (1) Finder sample: 61 unique AEA article pages in data/audit_scratch/aea (test.html duplicates 10.1257/aer.90.5.1160 and was excluded) have 134 citation_author slots and 105 non-empty citation_author_institution values. The 2002-2007 slice (18 pages) has 31 slots and only 2 non-empty values: 10.1257/000282802320189294 and 10.1257/000282802760015748. (2) Matching the same 61 DOIs to data/raw/crossref/pages gives 135 author slots, 134 with non-empty affiliation; 2002-2007 is 31 slots/30 affiliated, the only miss being 10.1257/000282802760015577 (Sherwin Rosen), where AEA is also empty. So AEA 2/31 vs Crossref 30/31 and 105/134 vs 134/134 reproduce. The extra Crossref slot is Cherry Bekaert on 10.1257/aer.112.6.2083 ("LLP, Nashville, Tennessee"), an author absent from the AEA page (0 authors), so Crossref's own-slot coverage is 134/135, not literally 134/134. (3) Corpus SQL (read-only): SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(TRIM(COALESCE(a.affiliation_raw,''))<>'') FROM authorships a JOIN papers p ON p.paper_id=a.paper_id WHERE p.content_type='article' -> 10,858 slots / 10,773 affiliated = 99.22%; per year 2002-2007: 364/358 (98.35%), 348/342 (98.28%), 348/341 (97.99%), 377/370 (98.14%), 373/364 (97.59%), 391/386 (98.72%). Parsing all six raw Crossref pages independently and restricting to the 4,844 article DOIs reproduces identical per-paper counts (0 mismatches); duplicates (101 slots, 0 affiliations) are correctly excluded by content_type='article'.

But the period claim and likely cause are wrong. Genuine same-template AEA pages for 2002 already in scratch carry full institutions: aea_10.1257_00028280260136192.html ("Department of Economics, University of California, Berkeley, CA 94720-3880"), ...0136246, ...0136264, v_art_10.1257_000282802760015603.html, v_strat_10_1257_000282802320189320.html. Deduping all AEA captures in scratch by DOI (109 unique DOIs; 0 inconsistent repeat captures) gives 43 DOIs/80 slots for 2002-2007 with AEA 13/80 non-empty: 2002 11/14 (78.6%), 2003 0/11, 2004 0/12, 2005 0/14, 2006 0/14, 2007 2/15 (13.3%); Crossref covers 79/80. All 61 sampled pages emit a citation_author_institution meta tag for every author slot (tag count == author count on 61/61 pages), so the template does emit the tag; the values are blank in AEA's CMS for many 2003-2006/2007 articles. Hence "AEA HTML templates for 2002-2007 do not emit citation_author_institution" is refuted, and "empty for 2002-2007" is false for 2002, whose values are full addresses, not abbreviations.

Scope/count: research articles 2002-2007 = 1,137 papers, 2,201 author slots; the corrected near-empty scope 2003-2007 = 944 papers, 1,837 author slots, where AEA coverage is 2/66 sampled slots (3.0%) and 2003-2006 is 0/51. The finder's 29 is only 31-2 in its own 31-slot convenience sample and understates the 2003-2007 exposure (1,837 slots) by ~60x. Crossref remains the right primary source (99.2% corpus-wide; 97.6-98.7% in 2002-2007), so the recommendation stands.
votes.notes: Directionally right, numerically exact for its sample, but the scope and root cause are overstated. Corrected scope is 2003-2007 rather than 2002-2007: in the expanded unique-DOI sample 2002 AEA pages cover 11/14 author slots with full institution strings, 2003-2006 cover 0/51, and 2007 covers 2/15. The realistic exposure is 1,837 research-article author slots in 2003-2007 (944 papers); the full 2002-2007 window has 2,201 slots. The likely_cause "templates do not emit citation_author_institution" is false: the tag is present on 61/61 sampled pages and on every author slot, with empty content only for many 2003-2007 articles. The recommendation to use Crossref publish-time affiliations as primary and AEA only as a cross-check remains valid; AEA's 2002 full addresses could also be a useful 2002 cross-check. Note Crossref rank-word coverage is only 6.2% (already documented), so affiliation strings alone do not solve career-stage inference; CV evidence is still required. The finding's full-sample 134/134 Crossref figure is exact only when aligned to AEA's 134 author slots; Crossref has one extra author on 10.1257/aer.112.6.2083.
